title: Beaubourg
label: RCA Records
overview:
Beaubourg is the fourth album Vangelis produced at Nemo Studios, London, and his last for RCA; it was released in July 1978, with Keith Spencer-Allen as recording engineer and Marlis Duncklau as assistant engineer. It is a concept album inspired by the Centre Georges Pompidou in Paris, the Beaubourg complex, which Vangelis visited in 1977; in a June 1979 interview he says he went back to London and recorded the album quickly and spontaneously, in a little less than a month. Wikipedia, citing Background Magazine and Synthtopia, says the music was improvised mainly on one or more Yamaha CS-80 synthesizers with a ring modulator used extensively, and Synthtopia hears pure tones turning into clangorous, distorted metallic noise, with brief melodies and a few quiet, plaintive tonal sections. The album is two long pieces, "Beaubourg, Part I" and "Beaubourg, Part II".

AllMusic's Steve McDonald calls it "difficult listening" and a "great dark synthesized tone poem" and gives it 2.5 stars out of 5, and Background Magazine's Henri Stirk rated the 2013 Esoteric Recordings reissue 2 out of 5. In the 1979 interview Vangelis says the record caused a scandal, with some people returning the disc, that he needed courage to release it, and that RCA had not believed in any of his four albums; he had by then moved to Polydor, and he says the album sold well. He promoted the release with a live appearance at the Pavillon de Paris on 19 June 1978. The track durations here are those of the rip, 17:57 and 20:45; Wikipedia lists 18:09 and 21:05 and MusicBrainz 17:53 and 20:42.

Section timestamps are measured on a rip of the CD and are approximate to ±5 seconds.

tracks.title: Beaubourg, Part I
tracks.role: Album role: The first of the album's two long pieces, a continuous sequence of loud, dark stretches, thin passages and sudden breaks that ends on a fast repeating pulse.

events.description: The sound starts after about a second and a half of silence, a mid-range texture at a moderate level that grows louder over the first half minute.
events.detail: Synthtopia describes the album as an abstract electronic tone poem in which recognisable melodies last a few moments before drifting into distorted, clangorous noise.

events.description: A loud, dark stretch led by a heavy low end, followed by a minute of alternating brighter and darker passages.
The low end mostly drops out and the level falls for about 45 seconds, leaving a thin mid-range texture; a loud, bright passage returns afterwards.
The sound fades away into about six seconds of near-silence, the first clear break in the piece; a full, loud texture then returns and builds.
The loudest stretch of Part I, about half a minute long, followed by a brief dip and a varied stretch of changing textures.
A steadier, moderately loud stretch with the low end mostly present, leading into a darker, heavier stretch with a rising low end.
The level drops to a very quiet stretch of about 15 seconds that ends in about three seconds of near-total silence.
The sound returns at full level within a fraction of a second, with a heavy low end, and grows darker and heavier over the next minute.
After a short dip and a moment of silence, a steady, mid-range-led texture at an almost constant level holds for about 45 seconds before the low end returns.
A loud, dark bed with a heavy, steady low end carries the next two and a half minutes, with changing layers above it and a brief brighter burst; the level then falls.
After about two seconds of silence, a fast, steady repeating pulse runs through the rest of the piece; the low end is absent at first and returns with a louder level.
The sound falls away over about six seconds and the piece ends, leaving a few seconds of silence at the end of the track.

tracks.title: Beaubourg, Part II
tracks.role: Album role: The closing half and the longer of the two pieces, nearly three minutes longer than Part I, more broken up by near-silent gaps and ending in a slow fade.

events.description: A quiet mid-range texture opens; the low end thickens and the sound becomes loud and bright within the first two minutes.
The loud passage fades into about eight seconds of near-silence, and the sound then returns abruptly at full level.
A thin, mid-range-led passage with little low end, broken by a few short silent breaks; the low end then returns quietly and the texture stays at a moderate level.
A dark, low-heavy passage with almost no high frequencies, ending in a fast repeating low pulse and a few seconds of near-silence.
The sound returns at full level and stays loud, bright and full for about a minute and a half, the loudest sustained stretch of Part II, then eases to a moderate level.
The sound breaks into short fragments with brief silent gaps and stays quiet and mid-range-led for about three minutes, with a quiet return of the low end and one loud burst.
A quiet, thin passage leaning to the high register, with almost no low end, followed by a short silence and a quiet low-end bed.
A short, steady pulse appears and the sound then thins to near-silence and returns quietly; the low end comes back at a louder level, with brief silent gaps.
A steady, fast, dark low-register pulse with almost no highs runs for about half a minute, and a second, shorter pulse leads into a loud, full stretch.
The high frequencies drop away and a dark, steady low-end bed carries the next two minutes, falling to a quiet drone before a slow swell and a brief silence.
After a fade to near-silence, the sound enters abruptly with a very heavy low end, and a steady, low-heavy passage holds for about a minute, with brighter mid-range layers appearing later.
The level falls and the texture thins to a quiet, low-heavy sound that fades to silence by about 20:43.
